capture: s1-dream-discover — the three decision surfaces, opened
surface: inspector instance (signed out, extension-clean); consent 'Reject all'

extraction_error_recorded.what_happened: A first pass clicked each of the three tabs and returned IDENTICAL content for all three — the sponsored hotel list.
extraction_error_recorded.why: The decision panels report offsetParent === null even when selected, so a 'first visible tabpanel' selector fell through to the results list every time.
extraction_error_recorded.why_this_is_recorded: Identical output from three different controls is a signature of extraction failure, not a product finding. Had it been written up it would have produced the false claim that Google's three decision surfaces show the same thing. Verified against aria-selected and per-panel text before recording anything.
extraction_error_recorded.correct_method: Enumerate ALL [role=tabpanel] nodes and read each by index; do not filter on visibility.

surface_1_where_to_stay.shape: Ranked neighbourhood list, each with a one-line reason and an 'Add area' action that filters the search.
surface_1_where_to_stay.verbatim: TOP AREAS — 1. Alfama: São Jorge Castle & live Fado music. 2. Bairro Alto: São Roque Church & happening nightlife. 3. Príncipe Real: Stylish shopping & Príncipe Real Garden.
surface_1_where_to_stay.what_it_answers: 'I don't know this city — where should I even be?' The reason is given per area, so the recommendation is explained rather than asserted.

surface_2_when_to_visit.shape: Seasonality prose plus weather and local events.
surface_2_when_to_visit.verbatim: Peak travel is Apr-Sep, when temperatures are warm. Jul-Aug is especially hot, sunny and dry. Indie Lisboa (Apr) is a film festival focusing on international... [Read more]
surface_2_when_to_visit.what_it_answers: 'When should I go, and what will it be like?' — a question asked BEFORE dates exist, which every transactional competitor requires as an input.

surface_3_what_youll_pay_STRONGEST.shape: Typical nightly price BY STAR CLASS, each with a range, the month it applies to, and the inventory count behind it.
verbatim: 2-star hotels €62 Typical — Usually €48-€75 per night in Sep — 51+ hotels
3-star hotels €102 Typical — Usually €76-€127 per night in Sep — 77+ hotels
surface_3_what_youll_pay_STRONGEST.what_it_answers: 'Is this a normal price, or am I being taken advantage of?'
surface_3_what_youll_pay_STRONGEST.why_it_is_the_strongest: This is the only surface observed anywhere in the round that directly addresses a first-time traveller's core anxiety — not knowing what normal looks like. It requires no booking, no account and no commitment, and it gives a RANGE plus the sample size behind it rather than a single number. It is an honesty device.

finding_F27.claim: Google Travel is the only product observed that tells a traveller what a normal price looks like before they search.
finding_F27.evidence: 'What you'll pay' gives typical nightly price by star class with an explicit range, month, and inventory count. Booking.com and Expedia captures contain no equivalent — both present prices only in the context of a specific property, anchored against a struck-through 'previous price'.
finding_F27.contrast_that_matters: Booking.com and Expedia both use price ANCHORING at the property level — 'The previous price was $571', 'Sale $185 off'. Anchoring tells you this deal is good relative to a number the seller chose. Google's typical-range tells you what the market actually costs. These are opposite epistemics: one is persuasion, one is orientation.
finding_F27.scope_limit: Three competitors. Whether any of the remaining fourteen offers an equivalent is untested.

our_product_decision_required: Decision required: 'what a normal price looks like' is the cheapest anti-anxiety feature observed in the round — no inventory, no supplier deal, no transaction required. Is it in Luma's first build?

Decision required: Google explains its neighbourhood recommendations with a reason per area. Booking.com and Expedia rank without explaining. Does Luma explain every recommendation, and can it, at ideation, without the data that produces the reason?

Decision required: 'When to visit' assumes dates are not yet chosen. Every transactional competitor REQUIRES dates as a search input. Luma's stage 1 is 'Dream & discover' — does its search accept an undecided traveller?
